items.definition:
reveal
The investigation will reveal the truth.

split
They decided to split the bill.

affect
The weather can affect your mood.

approve
The committee needs to approve the new plan.

arrest
The police decided to arrest the suspect.

to stretch out or prolong
We decided to extend our stay for another week.

to choose someone by voting
Citizens will elect a new president next year.

to recognize or establish the identity of
Can you identify the person in this photograph?

deliver
The postman will deliver the package tomorrow.

to put an end to the existence of something
The fire destroyed the old building.

to suggest or praise as suitable or good
I highly recommend this book.

to mention or allude to; to direct attention to
Please refer to the manual for more details.

to try to find or obtain something
They are seeking new opportunities abroad.

assign a job or role to (someone)
They decided to appoint her as the new manager.

do something or have qualities worthy of (reward or punishment)
You deserve a break after all that hard work.

to record; to sign up
You need to register for the course by Friday.

to confess; to allow entry
He had to admit he was wrong.

to take the place of
You need to replace the old battery with a new one.

to successfully bring about or reach
She worked hard to achieve her goals.

to have enough money to pay for
I can't afford a new car right now.

be inclined, look after
Prices tend to rise in the summer.

explain, characterize
Can you define the term 'democracy'?

to support or actively encourage
The campaign aims to promote healthy eating habits.

officially or legally prohibit
Smoking is banned in all public buildings.

to hit something hard; to fail suddenly
The car crashed into a tree.

to stop doing something
He decided to quit his job.

to say that you will not do or accept something
She refused to answer the question.

to experience something bad or unpleasant
He suffers from severe headaches.

to fasten or join one thing to another
Please attach your resume to the application form.

to take hold of something or someone suddenly and roughly
He grabbed his bag and ran out the door.

continue to live or exist
Only a few plants can survive in the desert.

take into one's family; formally accept
They decided to adopt a child.

point or direct; intend
He aimed the camera at the bird.

cause harm or damage to
He injured his knee playing football.

arrange or put in order
We need to organize the event.

make a solemn promise; use offensive language
I swear I will tell the truth.

successfully complete an academic degree
She will graduate from university next year.

make free of something undesirable
We need to get rid of this old furniture.

to be all around
Trees surround the old house.

to refuse to take notice of
Don't ignore my advice.

to save from a dangerous situation
The firefighters managed to rescue everyone from the burning building.

to move with urgent haste
We had to rush to catch the train.

to make someone unable to think clearly or understand
The instructions confused me, so I couldn't finish the task.

to protect from harm or danger
The lawyer tried to defend his client in court.

to give support, confidence, or hope to someone
Her parents always encourage her to study hard.

to give someone facts or information
Please inform me if there are any changes.

capture
The police managed to capture the suspect.

to stop working due to age
My grandfather plans to retire next year.

to resolve a dispute or to make a home
Let's try to settle this argument peacefully.

to make someone feel tired and uninterested
His long speech began to bore the audience.

to state that something is not true
He denied all the accusations.

to help or support someone or something
Can I assist you with your bags?

to fail to fulfill the hopes or expectations of
I hope I don't disappoint you with my performance.

to give work to someone; to make use of
The company employs over 500 people.

take part in
Everyone should participate in the discussion.

draw into the mouth; be bad (informal)
The baby continued to suck his thumb.

employ for wages; obtain the temporary use of
The company decided to hire a new manager.

to irritate or bother (someone)
His constant whistling began to annoy me.

to put or hide underground
They decided to bury the treasure in the garden.

to persuade (someone) to do something
I tried to convince him to join us.

to put in place for use
We need to install new software on the computer.

to speak to God
Many people pray for peace.

to give a task or duty
The teacher assigned homework to the students.

to annoy; to take the trouble to do something
Don't bother me when I'm working.
